stem:
Farid watches a frog sit on a sun-warmed rock beside a pond. Living parts of a habitat are biotic; non-living parts such as rock and sunlight are abiotic.

Which claim correctly classifies the frog–rock interaction?

options.text: It is biotic–abiotic, because a living frog interacts with a non-living rock.
It is biotic–biotic, because the frog and the rock are both treated as living.
It is abiotic–abiotic, because the rock and sunlight are both non-living.
It is not an interaction, because a frog never meets non-living parts of a habitat.

teacher.key_rationale: A living organism interacting with a non-living part is biotic–abiotic. Calling the rock living, swapping to only non-living pairs, or denying any meeting with abiotic parts miss that classification hinge.
